top.title: Florida turns recruiting momentum into commitment from 2027 OT Moreno Fisher
top.description: Florida has landed one of the fastest-rising offensive linemen in the 2027 class. Moreno Fisher , a 6-foot-7, 270-pound offensive tackle out of Cornelius (N.C.) Hough , has committed to Jon Sumrall and the Gators following his official visit to Gainesville. The former Virginia commit saw his recruitment take off this fall. Auburn , Florida and Florida State were among the major programs to extend offers after Fisher reopened his recruitment. But Florida made its move early, and the Gators never let up. Fisher first visited Gainesville in September for the Ole Miss game. That trip gave Florida momentum, and offensive line coach Phil Trautwein continued building on it. Now the Gators have landed another offensive lineman for their 2027 recruiting class. “The experience and the whole environment of that game was something crazy,” Fisher previously told Rivals. “It was a daytime game, and it was still packed out. No open seats in the crowd. It was a great experience, honestly.” That first visit helped Fisher see Florida differently. The atmosphere impressed him, but the coaching staff ultimately helped separate the Gators from the competition. Trautwein made Fisher a priority from the moment Florida offered. The Gators’ offensive line coach stayed in regular contact, explained his vision for Fisher’s development and established a strong relationship with the North Carolina standout. “I like Coach Trautwein a lot. He has coached some great offensive linemen. Since offering me, he has recruited me hard. He is a top coach.” Sumrall also made a strong impression. Fisher followed Florida’s progress throughout the season and liked how the Gators responded to adversity. “Coach Sumrall has done a great job,” Fisher said. “They have a great atmosphere at Florida. The crowd is great. It is a top SEC school and the coaches have them playing well.” Florida’s staff continued making Fisher feel wanted after his September visit. Sumrall, Trautwein and other staff members maintained weekly communication, and the Gators made an in-person stop to see Fisher ahead of his official visit. That consistent attention mattered. “Honestly, it’s because of how they make me feel, coming from a coaching staff standpoint and a player standpoint,” Fisher said. “They make me feel like a priority.” Fisher also took notice of the direction of the program. “Then the way they carry themselves so far this season, bouncing back from losses, responding. It’s all just right in front of me. I like what they are about.” By the time Fisher returned to Gainesville for his official visit, Florida had established itself as the program to beat. The Gators used that opportunity to finish the job. Fisher’s commitment gives Florida a massive offensive tackle prospect with considerable upside. At 6-foot-7 and 270 pounds, he brings the length and frame that college programs covet at the position.

top.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, has asked Nigerians to trust him to deliver a free, fair, credible and inclusive election next year, promising to not fail them This was as he said the commission is yet to recover from the trust deficit created by the technical glitches associated with the 2023 general election, and vowed that inaccurate polling unit results will not reach the INEC Result Viewing Portal IReV in 2027. Amupitan spoke on Thursday at Chatham House, London, at a dialogue held with the Kimpact Development Initiative (KDI) on the theme, “Nigeria’s 2027 Elections: Democratic Trajectory and Regional Stability Beyond the Ballot.” His Chief Press Secretary, Adedayo Oketola, said the INEC chairman noted that the controversies over the 2023 presidential election badly dented public confidence in the commission. “First, let me speak about what happened in 2023, which resulted in a significant trust deficit for INEC—damage so large that the Commission has not yet fully recovered from it,” he said. He said the commission’s audit after 2023 traced the worst result management failures to collation centres, not polling units. “In 2023, there were instances of inaccurate results or results with over-voting being uploaded onto IReV. We have now devised a technical safeguard: if a result is not accurate at the polling unit, it will not go to IReV at all. The moment a result appears on IReV, citizens can trust what they see. By eliminating inconsistencies at the source, collation will become a transparent formality”, he stated. The INEC chairman announced that the commission would hold a nationwide mock accreditation and voting exercise on November 28, 2026. “On the 28th of this month, we will conduct a mock accreditation and voting exercise across all states of the federation to simulate the presidential election and verify that we have gotten both accreditation and electronic result transmission right,” he said. Asked why Nigerians should trust his leadership, Amupitan who assumed office in October 2025, pointed to the off-cycle elections he had conducted. “Why must Nigerians trust me? Nigerians must trust me because, number one, I have conducted off-cycle elections—and observers agree that the recent election in Osun State marked a clear improvement,” he said. He listed the Anambra and Osun governorship elections, the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Area Council polls, the Ekiti governorship election and 16 legislative by-elections. The 2023 general election was a major lesson for Nigeria, and the Anambra election was another,” he said. top.title: Real Madrid complete their first signing of the 2027/28 season – report
top.description: Real Madrid complete their first signing of the 2027/28 season – report According to MARCA , Real Madrid have completed an agreement to sign Ghanaian midfielder Latif Issman from UD Logrones, with the youngster set to join Castilla next summer. The deal was finalised today, making the 20-year-old the club’s first acquisition for the 2027-28 campaign. Real Madrid tracking Issman since the summer Issman, who is represented by MS Sports, has been on Real Madrid’s radar since the summer. The Spanish capital club made an attempt to sign him towards the end of the summer window, but were unable to get the deal across the line. However, having missed out on his signing in the summer, Los Blancos stepped up their efforts in recent weeks and have now been successful in reaching an agreement with UD Logrones. The two clubs already have a working relationship, having negotiated the transfer of Manex Rezola to Valdebebas last winter. Issman’s current contract with UD Logrones runs until June 30, 2027, meaning his move to Real Madrid will coincide with the end of his existing deal. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Rising Football Pros (@risingfootballpros_gh) Previous reports suggested that the midfielder had a release clause worth €300,000 in his contract with Logrones. For now, it is unclear if Real Madrid have paid that sum or negotiated a lower fee, or will be signing Issman for free. Who is Latif Issman? Born on November 1, 2006, Issman began his development at SD Logrones before moving to UD Logrones at youth level. He made the step up to the senior squad in July 2025 and gradually established himself as an important part of the team. Unai Mendia gave him playing time in all four matches during the promotion play-offs. His involvement increased further following the club’s promotion to RFEF Primera Federacion , where he has featured in ten games, even registering one assist. The 20-year-old Ghanaian talent also has one appearance in the Copa del Rey this season. Latif Issman will be Real Madrid’s first signing for next summer. (Photo by Gonzalo Arroyo Moreno/Getty Images) As per the report, Real Madrid’s interest is understood to have been driven by Issman’s physical presence and ability to break opposition lines. The midfielder attracted offers from several clubs, but the Merengues moved decisively to secure his signature. He is viewed as a potential long-term option in the No. 8 role at Valdebebas. His ability to provide balance in a double pivot, while also making forward runs and contributing to attacks, makes him an appealing profile for Castilla. With his signing for Real Madrid now completed, the next step for Issman will be adapting to the demands of the club’s reserve team when he arrives next summer.

top.title: Arsenal hold Barca to women's Champions League draw
top.description: Barcelona's Norwegian forward Caroline Graham Hansen pulled the holders level with Arsenal before the hour mark (MANAURE QUINTERO) Arsenal earned an impressive 1-1 draw at women's Champions League holders Barcelona on Thursday in a league phase clash between two of the competition's heavyweights. Caroline Graham Hansen secured four-time champions Barca, who have reached the final six seasons running, a point after Frida Maanum fired visitors Arsenal into a surprise lead at Camp Nou. The Gunners beat Barcelona in the 2025 final in Lisbon in the teams' last meeting and, despite Renee Slegers's team's domestic struggles, dug deep to deliver on the big stage again. The draw leaves Barca, second, level on 10 points with leaders Lyon after four matches, while the Londoners are fourth, level on eight points with third-place Bayern Munich and Chelsea. Two-time winners Arsenal had a golden opportunity in the opening stages when Caitlin Foord broke into the box but Irene Paredes blocked brilliantly. The rebound fell to Alessia Russo, who headed against the post from point-blank range, but appeared to be offside. Barcelona took control after that, with Graham Hansen and Sydney Schertenleib forcing Arsenal's Misa Rodriguez into two saves at her near post. The visitors, who are languishing in sixth in the English top flight, rode out the barrage and nosed ahead through Maanum after 22 minutes. Barcelona goalkeeper Cata Coll saved well from Foord but Norwegian midfielder Maanum reacted quickest to latch on to the rebound and slot home. Graham Hansen ran Arsenal left-back Taylor Hinds ragged but Barca could not break through before the interval. Claudia Pina fired narrowly wide after a burst inside from the left and Paredes looped a header over the crossbar. Graham Hansen's header clipped the post just before the break as Pere Romeu's Barca went in frustrated, but the Norwegian winger pulled them level before the hour mark. Esmee Brugts found Graham Hansen in the box and she cut inside Steph Catley and whipped a strike into the top left corner. Russo might have put Arsenal back in front but hammered over when well placed after being teed up by substitute Olivia Smith. Arsenal resisted Barcelona pressure in the final stages to end the hosts' 100 percent start to the competition. rbs/ea

top.title: Providence to host women's basketball franchise in spring 2027
top.description: PROVIDENCE — Women's professional basketball is coming to Amica Mutual Pavilion beginning in May. That's when the UpShot League will debut downtown, with Providence officially awarded an expansion franchise at a Thursday morning press conference in the venue's front lobby. Managing partner Mark Walsh said the Providence franchise will play its home opener May 13, part of a 28-game schedule that will run through the spring and summer. The league debuted in 2026 with four teams and is in the process of adding new markets ahead of its 2027 return. More: Rhode Island’s new UFL team has a name. Meet the Breakers "This is your team," Walsh said. "We want this to be your team. We are not asking for any money from the community — we are asking you for support." Gov. Dan McKee, Providence Mayor Brett Smiley and House Speaker Joseph Shekarchi were among the state political delegation gathered Thursday. They joined several executives from the Rhode Island Convention Center — CEO Dan McConaghy, chairman Ernest Almonte and general manager Larry Lepore. The state's basketball community was represented by former Providence College basketball star Ernie DiGregorio, former Johnston High and Friars standout Chelsea Marandola and former Providence players Harold Starks and Quinton Burton. "Providence is a great basketball city and it just became greater because of today's announcement," Smiley said. Walsh attempted to position the Providence franchise as a professional replacement for the Connecticut Sun, which played its last WNBA game 48 days ago and will relocate to Houston. Providence was among the cities that made both a presentation and formal offer to that team's owners in an attempt to keep them in the region. Discussions soon pivoted to the UpShot delegation while attempting to fill more dates downtown outside the traditional fall and winter schedules played by the Providence College men and Providence Bruins. "This team will give women a great opportunity to continue improving their basketball skills and to grow within the sport," Almonte said. "It will give players, coaches and referees a stage to showcase their talents and potentially move up to the WNBA." McKee attended the press conference with his daughter, Kara, a former player in their hometown of Cumberland. She was part of the first all-girls league in their community and developed into a state champion prior to her entry into high school. McKee asked her to recruit five classmates while starting their first team. That number eventually grew to more than 100 girls participating. "Full circle to be standing here at the AMP," McKee said. "A win for women's sports, a win for our capital city and a win for Rhode Island. Welcome." What is the UpShot League? The UpShot League was founded by Florida-based Zawyer Sports & Entertainment in January 2025. Investors include women's basketball greats Cheryl Miller, Ann Meyers Drysdale and Tamika Catchings and former Florida standout Patric Young. Jacksonville

top.title: Reeling Oregon Ducks remain positive, committed to the grind
top.description: EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks . One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished. Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season. “One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity,” sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said. After his team’s 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward. On Wednesday, he said the team has elevated its work ethic and embraced accountability. “I’ve been proud of the way that they’ve worked,” Lanning said. “I don’t see a lot of hanging heads, right? I think that’s challenging, too, especially when you’re young, to not lose a little bit of gusto and not lose a little bit of belief.” Oregon linebacker Devon Jackson (#9) drops UCLA running back Wayne Knight (#3) for no gain as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian The Ducks, who host Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) at 8 p.m. Saturday, responded well to adversity following a 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State on Sept. 12. Oregon won its next two games, including a 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. That victory seemed to give the Ducks a fresh start. But two weeks later, they lost to the Bruins and dropped out of the rankings. Now, Oregon must run the table to have a legitimate shot at the College Football Playoff, which seemed like a given for a team that returned most of its starters from last year’s semifinal squad. He added that the team’s goals remain attainable, and team leaders have worked to encourage togetherness and mutual trust. “If you can’t trust your teammate, then everything ain’t going to form in the way that it’s supposed to,” he said. top.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
top.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. top.title: Oregon has 3 quarterbacks who could start Saturday. Illinois has a freshman who's never started before
top.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. top.description: The Detroit Tigers have agreed to a one-year deal worth $11 million with relief pitcher Emilio Pagan, a deal the New York Post first reported . Pagan is 35 and turns 36 during the 2027 MLB season, and he is the favorite to take over the ninth inning in Detroit after the Tigers declined their 2027 club option on Kenley Jansen . Pagan declined a $10 million player option with the Cincinnati Reds for the 2027 season. The move got him at least $1 million more than the option he turned down. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Emilio Pagan missed 47 games with a hamstring strain last season Even though the Tigers appear to have found their closer for the 2027 MLB season, Pagan missed 47 games during the 2026 MLB season with Cincinnati because of a left hamstring strain. He was carted off the field after a single pitch on May 5 , and the Reds did not have him back on the active roster until June 30 . Pagan pitched in 45 games for Cincinnati last season. His record was 5-1 with a 3.38 ERA . In 42.2 innings pitched, he gave up 33 hits and 16 runs, walked 11 batters and struck out 45. His WHIP was 1.03, and he recorded 25 saves on 28 attempts. The case for the signing is in what he did after he got healthy. From July 1 on, Pagan put up a 1.88 ERA over his final 30 appearances and converted every one of his 19 save chances. top.title: Nelly Korda shoots bogey-free 63 in return at The Annika
top.description: Nelly Korda opened The Annika with a bogey-free 7-under 63 on Thursday at Pelican Golf Club. It was her first start since the Solheim Cup in mid-September. The world No. 1 made five birdies on the front nine to turn in 30. She added birdies at Nos. 14 and 17 on the way in and finished two shots behind playing partner Hye-Jin Choi, who shot 61 to take the early lead. Korda skipped the LPGA’s four-event Asia swing. She said she was burned out when the Solheim Cup matches ended in the Netherlands, and decided to take a five-day vacation in Greece. After that, she recharged at home. Korda said her favorite things during the break were cooking, sleeping in her own bed and going to the gym. "Just getting in a routine of being like a normal kind of human being," she said. "I think that's what reenergizes my batteries the most." Korda, 28, has dealt with neck problems in recent seasons and is comfortable trimming her schedule. “My body just can’t do that,” she said of the 30-event seasons some rookies play. “Once I start to feel something I just have to take that break.” She said her familiarity with Jason McDede, her caddie of eight years, gave her comfort coming back. “He knows exactly what to say, and we switch right back into that routine,” she said. Additionally, her putting coach, David Angelotti, is with her this week. Korda said their work did not change during the break and that she likes to keep things simple in her camp. “I don’t want to know all the numbers,” she said. “I just want to know a few simple keys.” Korda's return comes at a consequential time. She clinched her second Rolex Player of the Year award last week , which gave her 26 of the 27 points needed for the LPGA Hall of Fame. A win this week or at next week’s CME Group Tour Championship would earn her the last point. She would be the third-youngest player to enter the LPGA’s Hall of Fame , behind Lydia Ko and Inbee Park. Korda has won four times in 2026, including the Chevron Championship and the U.S. Women’s Open. She has good memories at the Annika, having won it three times, but commented that the Hall of Fame is not on her mind. “Is the Hall of Fame something I’m really looking at? Not at all,” she said. “I mean, I’m just focusing on being competitive and trying to give it my all. ... After that, everything else is out of my control." Well rested and inspired, Nelly Korda eyes Hall of Fame at Annika Korda hasn’t played a regular LPGA event since August but returns with some inspired footwear at this week’s Annika. nigeria.title: Scaloni to stay on as Argentina coach until 2030 World Cup
nigeria.description: Lionel Scaloni on Thursday agreed to stay on as coach of Argentina’s national football team until after the 2030 World Cup, ending the doubts that had been swirling since this year’s World Cup final defeat. Scaloni’s decision to renew his contract was announced by Argentine Football Association president Claudio Tapia at a press conference with the 48-year-old manager. Scaloni, who took the Albiceleste to victory at the 2022 tournament in Qatar, told reporters he was as enthusiastic as “on day one”. “A new project begins now,” he said a month after Lionel Messi, the team’s leading light for 20 years, bowed out of international football. Tapia said that Scaloni would be the Argentina manager with the most World Cups under his belt by the time his contract ended. Scaloni had cast doubt on his future with the team after Argentina’s 1-0 defeat by Spain in a bad-tempered July 19 World Cup final in New Jersey. He has been coach for eight years, taking over in September 2018, after a traumatic World Cup in Russia, where Argentina were eliminated in the round of 16. Scaloni took over one of the most prestigious jobs in football without any prior experience and built the team into one widely considered the best in Argentine history. Besides the 2022 World Cup he coached Argentina to two Copa America titles, in 2021 and 2024. He now faces the task of taking the team forward without his 39-year-old talisman Messi. “What must remain is this team spirit, this feeling of unity among the players and the people,” he said after losing the final to Spain. nigeria.description: United States head coach Mauricio Pochettino is set to be appointed as the new manager of Manchester United after the struggling English giants sacked Michael Carrick on Thursday. Pochettino is expected to leave his role with the USA following their two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final on Saturday and Tuesday in a move that will see United trigger a release clause worth some $10 million to secure the Argentine’s services. Pochettino, who signed a contract extension to remain with the United States through to the 2030 World Cup just three months ago, is due to hold a pre-match press conference on Friday. Former United captain Carrick led the team to an impressive third-place finish in the Premier League last season, but they have taken just eight points from 10 games in the current campaign and are in the relegation zone. nigeria.title: 2027: Tinubu will lose if he contests against anybody picked on street — Dalung
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye African Democratic Congress (ADC) chieftain Solomon Dalung has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu would lose the 2027 election even if his opponent were “anybody picked on the street,” arguing that the President was afraid of facing voters. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Dalung made the prediction while responding to a question about how the opposition could overcome the APC’s resources amid the current internal leadership and legal crisis in the ADC. He nevertheless insisted the party was ready to challenge Tinubu at the ballot. “Since my experience in politics, like I always say, Nigerians, I was brought into politics at a much tender age. I have never seen a weak president in an election like Bola Ahmed Tinubu. If you drag anybody on the street and put him on a ballot at a contest with Tinubu, he will defeat him,” Dalung said. He claimed Tinubu was apprehensive about the election despite having been in office for four years, and challenged the President and APC to let the contest be decided by voters. “Bola Tinubu is so scared, having been in office for four years, he is so scared of election. And all we are seeing in ADC, let’s meet at the ballot. You claim it was the ballot that brought you to power, let’s meet at the ballot,” he said. Dalung also accused the APC of obstructing opposition parties’ campaign activities, alleging that venues had been closed, hotels taken over and party offices sealed. He compared the situation with the 2014 election period, saying the APC would have been left with few places to campaign if it had faced similar restrictions then. “Nobody will be blamed except Tinubu. Why? Because I mean, in the history of Nigeria, we have seen opposition parties contest election, but we have never seen this type of situation. If the PDP in 2014 were closing venues for rallies and taking over hotels, sealing party offices, the APC would have no place to campaign except the streets,” he said. He argued that moving the opposition onto the streets would not weaken its campaign, claiming those attending its gatherings were genuine supporters rather than people hired to fill rallies. “Now, for Tinubu and his APC to move the opposition on pit, they have lost the election. This is because the people we are having on the street are organic followers. Those are the Nigerians that will vote. They are not rented crowds from all over the federation,” Dalung said. nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Italy defender Marco Materazzi says the death of Spanish striker Jesus de Miguel after an on-field collision made him reflect on the headbutt he suffered from Zinedine Zidane in the 2006 World Cup final. Materazzi said the incident, one of football’s most infamous World Cup moments, still troubled him 20 years later. He told Italian newspaper La Gazzetta dello Sport that De Miguel’s death made him grateful he had escaped serious injury. “The death of Jesus de Miguel made me thank God that nothing had happened to me,” Materazzi said in an interview published on Thursday. De Miguel, a Tenerife striker, died after colliding with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a Segunda Division match earlier this month. Zidane, then captain of France, was sent off for headbutting Materazzi in the chest during the 2006 final, which Italy won on penalties. Zidane, now France coach, said last month he was not proud of the headbutt but did not regret it. Materazzi said he and Zidane appeared to put the episode behind them when they met before a match in 2010, although Zidane later disputed Materazzi’s account of the encounter. “When he saw me, he hesitated a little, he even turned to walk back,” Materazzi said. “But I approached him and shook his hand: ‘I’m glad we’re meeting here, where nobody can see us.’ “He replied: ‘Don’t worry, these things happen, it’s all in the past.’ It’s a shame he later denied everything, saying he thought I was a fan.” France are scheduled to play Italy in the Nations League later on Thursday. nigeria.title: Tinubu’s economic reforms key to sustainable security, says Dare
nigeria.description: Former Minister of Youth and Sports Development, Sunday Dare, has said President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms and social interventions constitute an important part of a sustainable national security strategy, arguing that insecurity cannot be tackled through military operations alone. Dare, who disclosed this in a post on his X platform on Thursday, said economic development, effective governance and social inclusion were critical to addressing the underlying conditions that fuel insecurity. He observed that public discussions on national security often focused largely on military interventions, while overlooking the structural impact of economic policies and social programmes on the factors that sustain insecurity. According to him, states with poor developmental indices often record high levels of fragility, reinforcing the need to complement military operations with investments in development and effective governance. According to him, providing legitimate pathways to education and economic opportunities could reduce the vulnerability of young people to recruitment by insurgents and other violent groups. He described education not merely as a social investment but also as a long-term investment in national security. On local government autonomy, Dare said adequately resourced and accountable councils could strengthen government presence in communities through improved public services and development initiatives. He argued that responsive governance at the grassroots would reduce the opportunities for violent non-state actors to exploit poorly governed communities and public disaffection. The former minister also said improved FAAC allocations could enhance the capacity of state and local governments to invest in infrastructure, education, healthcare, employment and other essential services. nigeria.title: 2027: Opposition parties lack experience to govern Nigeria, says Ambode
nigeria.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Former Lagos State Governor, Akinwunmi Ambode, has criticised opposition parties seeking to unseat the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 general elections, saying they lack the political experience and leadership depth required to govern Nigeria. Ambode specifically mentioned the African Democratic Congress (ADC), the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and other opposition platforms, arguing that the APC had greater political experience and ideological consistency. He spoke at the APC East Senatorial District rally held at Epe Recreational Ground, Epe, Lagos State, where he canvassed support for President Bola Tinubu, the party’s Lagos governorship candidate, Dr Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, and other APC candidates ahead of the 2027 elections. Ambode said the APC had remained consistent in its political identity, unlike some politicians who, according to him, frequently moved from one political party to another. “APC is our party. We are a collective of the progressives. We have been consistent and delivering for the party. Over the years, we have remained with the progressives and we do not move from one party to another like other people,” he said. Describing the APC as a party connecting the country’s past, present and future, the former governor argued that its political experience placed it in a different position from opposition parties seeking to take over the reins of government. He also credited Tinubu’s political vision and record as Lagos governor with contributing to the state’s economic and infrastructural development, particularly its emergence as a major investment destination. Ambode said the foundations laid during Tinubu’s tenure as governor helped create an environment for financial institutions and corporate organisations to establish and expand their operations in Lagos. “Whether you like him or not, he is a visionary leader. If not for Tinubu, who laid the foundation for the Lagos of today, all the financial firms that have their headquarters in Lagos would have been struggling to survive. But today, his vision has assisted the country to remain an investor destination,” he said. He urged Lagos residents and Nigerians across different social and economic backgrounds to support the APC in the forthcoming elections. Ambode also appealed to members of the Igbo community living in Lagos and other parts of the country to consider national unity and their economic interests when making political choices. “To my Igbo brothers, wherever you live and get your prosperity, that is where you should call home. nigeria.title: I won’t leave England before Euro 2028 —Tuchel
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Thomas Tuchel has ruled out leaving England for a club job before Euro 2028, saying he wants to see out his contract and complete what he calls “unfinished business” with the national team. According to ESPN, Tuchel said there was “no release clause” in his England contract and “no intention” of leaving before the tournament. His comments come amid Manchester United’s move to replace Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino. “I signed a contract; I want to stay until the Euros. I want to do the Euros. We have unfinished business,” Tuchel said. The German succeeded Gareth Southgate in 2025 and signed a two-year extension in February, keeping him in charge through Euro 2028. Tuchel said he was “open for everything” once his contract ends, including staying with England, but confirmed he eventually wants to return to club management. “Yes, definitely,” he said when asked if he would return to club football. “I miss the 50 matches. I miss these two minutes when everything is done.” Tuchel said he also understood the pressures of the club game, where matches come every few days. He said he was grateful for his England role and the freedom to work with his staff. “I’m very grateful for what I have here because I know how rare it is to be in love with your team and to have the trust and to be able to work freely with your coaching staff, which I am,” he said. Tuchel also said he felt aligned with the Football Association from their first discussions and valued the trust of chief executive Mark Bullingham and chief football officer Dan Ashworth. “That’s what you look for as a coach,” he said. “I love my group of players. I love my staff, and I have bosses who trust me and are happy with the way we do things, so it’s a lot. “I appreciate it a lot, so it’s in a good place, I’m in a good place, and I love the players. I miss my players, and I miss my team, and I miss the 50 matches that I’m not involved in a year. “But I’m desperate to win the Nations League and to play and try to win the Euros.” The post I won’t leave England before Euro 2028 —Tuchel appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Benue State Executive Council has approved a total of N5.2 billion for the implementation of the second phase of the Nigeria Community Action for Resilience and Economic Stimulus (NG-CARES 2.0) programme and the payment of 12 months’ outstanding salary arrears owed academic staff of tertiary institutions in the state. He listed some of the beneficiary communities as Ihugh, Bako, Abaki, Tse-Alia, Mbausu, Ngehe, Hembe and Anhyula. On NG-CARES 2.0, the Commissioner for Finance, Mr Michael Oglegba, explained that the programme had previously supported rural communities through borehole projects, renovation of schools, provision of health facilities, cash transfers and business support. nigeria.title: Sokoto approves ₦6.12bn for nine UBEC model schools
nigeria.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO – The Sokoto State Government has approved ₦6.12 billion for the construction of nine Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC) prototype schools across the state’s three senatorial districts. The government also approved additional funds for the rehabilitation and construction of mosques and the development of Islamic educational institutions across the state. The approvals were among the major decisions reached at Wednesday’s State Executive Council meeting, presided over by Governor Ahmed Aliyu at the Government House, Sokoto. Briefing journalists after the meeting, the Commissioner for Budget and Economic Planning, Dr Bashir Achida, said the nine UBEC prototype schools would be distributed equally among the three senatorial districts, with three schools allocated to each district. He said the initiative was aimed at expanding access to quality basic education, improving the learning environment and providing modern facilities for pupils, particularly in communities requiring better school infrastructure. Achida said the investment was in line with Governor Aliyu’s commitment to transforming the education sector under his administration’s Nine-Point SMART Agenda. On religious infrastructure, the council approved ₦221,548,705.25 for the rehabilitation of Achida Central Juma’at Mosque and ₦154,941,290 for the rehabilitation of Sabon Birni Central Juma’at Mosque. It also approved ₦98,242,007.50 for the construction of five daily prayer mosques in the Kwamberu area and ₦285,125,650.92 for the rehabilitation of Tureta Central Juma’at Mosque in Tureta Local Government Area. Similarly, ₦230,660,473.19 was approved for the rehabilitation of Kuppa Juma’at Mosque in the Gidan Sauro area. In the area of Islamic education, the council approved ₦166,982,489 for the construction of classrooms and sanitation facilities at Raddul Azzam Quranic School in Achida. Another ₦297,655,995.50 was approved for the construction of an Islamic school in Sabon Garin Tudun Wada area of Sokoto South Local Government Area. The commissioner further disclosed that ₦53,937,500 was approved for the provision of carpets at Gada Central Juma’at Mosque to improve facilities for congregational prayers. Achida said the approvals reflected the administration’s commitment to interventions in critical sectors, particularly basic education, religious development and community infrastructure. The projects, when completed, are expected to expand access to educational facilities, improve existing religious institutions and provide additional infrastructure for learning and worship across the state’s three senatorial districts. nigeria.title: Edo pharmacists, consumer committee clash over drug inspections
nigeria.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY – The Edo State chapter of the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) has disagreed with the state Consumer Protection Committee (CPC) over the legality of the committee’s alleged entry into pharmaceutical premises to inspect and confiscate suspected expired, adulterated and counterfeit drugs. The pharmacists accused the committee of exceeding its statutory powers by conducting inspections, seizing pharmaceutical products and imposing fines on operators, insisting that the regulation of pharmacy practice is governed by federal laws. Addressing journalists in Benin City on Thursday on behalf of the Association of Community Pharmacists of Nigeria (ACPN), an arm of the PSN, the state president, Pharm. Chris Oisakede, said pharmacists had established procedures for handling expired drugs in collaboration with the Ministry of Health and the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC). Oisakede explained that expired medicines were not supposed to be discarded indiscriminately because of the dangers they posed to public health. “An expired drug is dangerous and poisonous, so they are usually gathered and handed over to NAFDAC, which has the protocols for destroying them,” he said. Flanked by other ACPN executives, Oisakede maintained that the CPC lacked the statutory authority to inspect, supervise or regulate pharmacy practice in the country. “For the avoidance of doubt, the Edo State CPC has no jurisdiction or authority, whether directly or indirectly, to enter, inspect, supervise or regulate the practice of pharmacy in Nigeria in any manner whatsoever. “Pharmacy practice in Nigeria, in all its aspects and ramifications, is governed by applicable federal legislation,” he said. He described community pharmacies as important healthcare facilities, noting that pharmacists counsel patients, promote the rational use of medicines, support treatment adherence, identify medicine-related problems and provide medicine safety information. The PSN consequently called on the committee to stop what it described as unauthorised pharmaceutical inspections, raids, harassment, seizures and sealing of premises, as well as the imposition of penalties where it could not establish clear statutory authority. However, reacting to the allegations, the CPC chairman, Osaro Culture Iyamu, defended the committee’s enforcement activities, citing Section 8 of the Counterfeit and Fake Drugs and Unwholesome Processed Foods (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act as the legal basis for its operations. Iyamu said the provision empowered him to enter premises where there were reasonable grounds to suspect violations of the law, inspect products and examine their packaging, as well as take samples for examination. He added that the law also authorised the seizure of counterfeit, adulterated, banned or fake drugs, confiscation of unwholesome processed food products and sealing of premises connected with suspected offences. nigeria.title: One dead, four wounded in Washington shooting
nigeria.description: One person was killed and four others wounded after a gunman opened fire in an upscale neighbourhood of Washington, DC, on Thursday before barricading himself inside his apartment and taking his own life, police said. The shooting, which occurred about a mile north of the White House, triggered a massive security response, with dozens of police vehicles deployed to the scene and helicopters hovering overhead. Washington’s interim police chief, Jeffery Carroll, told reporters that the gunman shot and killed one person at a fitness centre attached to his apartment building before wounding four others. He said the suspect subsequently barricaded himself inside his apartment and fired at least twice at police officers through the apartment door before shooting himself. The suspect, whose identity was not immediately disclosed, was pronounced dead at the scene. Carroll said preliminary information suggested that the gunman had been involved in “some sort of a conflict” with the homeowners association of the apartment building in the Logan Circle neighbourhood. One of the four injured victims was in critical condition, while the injuries sustained by the others did not appear to be life-threatening, the police chief said. Washington Mayor Muriel Bowser condemned the incident as a “senseless act of gun violence” and disclosed that the White House had been briefed on the shooting. The incident occurred during the busy morning rush hour, causing major traffic disruptions as police cordoned off streets around the area. Police evacuated some residents from nearby buildings, while others were instructed to remain indoors. The Washington Sun quoted a member of the VIDA Fitness gym as saying he was exercising on a treadmill when the shooting began. Michael Carney said he heard a “pop” before noticing a person lying on the gym floor with a gunshot wound to the head. “Everyone was kind of just hiding behind planters and stuff,” Carney told the newspaper. Logan Circle is one of Washington’s most expensive neighbourhoods, known for its upscale restaurants and nightlife venues. The area is also located a short distance from several foreign embassies. nigeria.title: Budget Minister challenges LGs to justify monthly allocations
nigeria.description: By Luminous Jannamike & Folarin Kehinde ABUJA – The Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, Senator Abubakar Atiku Bagudu, has challenged local governments to justify their monthly Federation Account allocations by turning them into tangible development rather than merely sharing the money. Bagudu said councils must identify economic opportunities in their communities, attract investments and create wealth instead of depending solely on statutory allocations. He spoke on Thursday in Abuja at the 9th annual national conference of the Association of Local Government Vice Chairmen of Nigeria (ALGOVC), themed, “Strengthening Local Government Control for Effective National Security and Economic Growth”. Bagudu said the Federal Government was adopting a bottom-up approach through the Renewed Hope Ward Development Plan to identify local resources, investment opportunities and development needs. “Local government is not just an administrative centre that should disburse money coming from the Federation Account. That is a big error that we have been making in the past. “It is a centre that should draw attention to the blessings and the prosperity and the opportunities and potentials that are in that local government, and appropriately support that local government,” he said. He urged councillors to identify the economic potential of their wards, adding that systematic mapping would provide data for attracting investors and developing practical economic plans. Bagudu identified agriculture, fisheries and livestock as sectors capable of transforming local economies but constrained by poor farming methods, inadequate inputs and outdated practices. Citing an estimated 42 million Nigerian households engaged in agriculture, he said improved productivity could raise household incomes and stimulate economic growth. He urged vice-chairmen to identify challenges in their councils and present evidence-based demands to the Federal Government and development partners. Earlier, ALGOVC National Chairperson, Amb. Uju Okolo, called for unity, accountability and inclusive leadership, pledging to promote justice, restore confidence and ensure no member was left behind. The conference also took a political turn when the association’s Board of Trustees Chairman, Hon. Lawrence Onuchukwu, moved a motion endorsing President Bola Tinubu for a second term in 2027. Seconded by Okolo, the motion was adopted through a voice vote. The association also pledged support for the ruling party at the federal and state levels and appealed to Tinubu to reappoint Bagudu as minister if re-elected. nigeria.title: 2027: INEC to simulate presidential election in nationwide mock vote
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) plans to conduct a nationwide mock accreditation and voting exercise on November 28 to test preparations for the 2027 general elections, Chairman Joash Amupitan has said. Amupitan announced the plan at a conference at Chatham House in London on Thursday, held to discuss “Democratic trajectory beyond the ballot” ahead of the elections. He said the exercise would simulate the forthcoming presidential election and test the commission’s readiness to transmit results. “On the 28th of this month, we are planning a mock accreditation and voting across all the states in Nigeria, so that we simulate a presidential election and just be sure that we have gotten it right and that there will be transmission of result,” Amupitan said. He also said the commission had reviewed lessons from previous elections and taken steps to address identified problems, citing recent off-cycle elections, including those in Anambra and Osun, as examples of improvements in the electoral process. “Nigerians must trust me because I’ve done off-cycle elections, and you agreed the last election in Osun State, there was improvement, and I said every election is a lesson. 2023 election was a great lesson for Nigeria. The one we had in Anambra was another. So we’ve learned certain things, and as a commission, we sat down to address some of those issues, and we have taken steps one after the other,” he said. Amupitan said INEC was working to improve logistics so voting and result declaration could be completed promptly as he pointed to the Anambra election, where results were declared the day after voting. “We are trying to improve on logistics to ensure that everything is done within the day, and then result. Look at the way we did an Anambra election. By the following day, we declared the result,” he said. He also cited recent off-cycle elections in the Federal Capital Territory and Osun, where he said results were declared the following day and voters observed the functioning of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and the transmission of results. “In FCT, the same thing. In Osun, that used to be a serious problem, that the whole world thought that the whole country will collapse with Osun election the following day, the result was declared, and everybody saw the functioning of B-VAS and the transmission of results,” Amupitan added. He said the mock exercise and other measures were intended to prevent a repeat of past problems, adding that transparency and the ability to audit the process were essential. “So those are things and steps that we have taken to ensure that we don’t go back to the mistake of the past. nigeria.description: Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has accused President Bola Tinubu of using political alliances to advance his political interests rather than promote national unity, saying the administration has failed to deliver the governance he expected when he supported Tinubu in the 2023 presidential election. Makinde, in a statement published on his RESET Nigeria website on Thursday, said he initially supported Tinubu because he believed the president would bring Nigerians together to build a government of national unity and competence. He, however, said his assessment of the administration had changed three years into its tenure, prompting his decision to challenge Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election. “I supported President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in 2023. Today, I am running against him in the 2027 presidential election,” he said. “Some people have asked what changed. Others believe there must have been a personal disagreement between us. “I understand why they would think that. He said he had become increasingly concerned about four major issues under the Tinubu administration: economic stability without economic development, governing by excuses, the pursuit of political power at the expense of national unity, and economic reforms without adequate protection for Nigerians. On the economy, Makinde acknowledged improvements in some macroeconomic indicators but argued that such gains had not sufficiently translated into better living conditions for ordinary Nigerians. “I acknowledge the improvements in some macroeconomic indicators under this administration. “But government revenues and external reserves mean little to ordinary Nigerians if those gains do not translate into productive businesses, jobs, better incomes and improved living conditions,” he said. According to him, Nigerians should not be made to endure the current level of hardship while waiting for the benefits of economic reforms to materialise. nigeria.title: ‘Your Sacrifice For A New Nigeria Won’t Be In Vain,’ Obi Assures Nigerians, Condemns Lagos Attack

business.title: Binance Says It Has Fully Covered the $6.34 Billion Hack With Company Funds
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Says It Has Fully Covered the $6.34 Billion Hack With Company Funds Binance said Thursday it has completed coverage of the $6.34 billion Oct. 29 hack from company funds, two weeks after the largest crypto theft on record, even as withdrawals continue to reopen in phases. In a Thursday announcement, the exchange wrote that it “has completed coverage of assets impacted in the security incident” and published a new proof-of-reserves snapshot. It repeated the same message on X. That wording matters. Coverage means Binance has replaced the affected tokens from its own books, not that it has recovered the stolen coins from the attackers. The exchange said it committed more than $6.34 billion in company funds and bought the affected tokens through market and over-the-counter channels, drawing on a partial deployment of its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), a portion of its futures insurance fund above the level required under its risk-management framework, and its corporate treasury. Binance has also committed to replenishing SAFU to about $1 billion after that partial draw, a step it said would keep the fund fully resourced as an emergency user-protection reserve. A very small number of tokens the exchange no longer lists were also affected. Binance said those holdings will be handled under its delisting process and that users who hold them will be covered. A wider proof-of-reserves snapshot, but no independent check yet Binance took a new proof-of-reserves snapshot at 00:00 UTC on Nov. 12, or 7 p.m. Eastern on Wednesday, covering 198 tokens. That is a sharp jump from the 10 tokens included in the Oct. 31 snapshot published in the days after the breach. The new figures are now posted on the exchange’s proof-of-reserves website. The snapshot, Binance said, “provides an updated view of assets that are fully accounted for.” Users cannot yet check that claim themselves. The exchange said the full zero-knowledge proof will take about 40 to 50 hours to generate because of the computational workload. After that, users holding the affected tokens “will be able to independently verify that their assets are backed at a minimum of 1:1.” Until the proof is ready, the 1:1 backing is Binance’s statement, not something customers can confirm on their own. Withdrawals are still coming back in phases Thursday’s update does not reopen the platform all at once. Binance said it continues to reopen withdrawals in phases and will share further details once they are confirmed. The exchange first reopened withdrawals on Nov. 1, starting with bitcoin and then expanding to other networks, and has kept the restart on a phased timetable since then. The announcement also does not say how much of the stolen assets have been retrieved, and it does not name an attacker. Covering customer balances leaves that recovery question unanswered. The Tel Aviv-listed lender described the service as a first for Israel’s banking system in a Nov. 11 statement. Customers will be able to trade the two assets alongside stocks and bonds, without opening an account at an outside exchange or managing a separate digital wallet. The offer is limited to private, not corporate, customers who are Israeli residents, 18 or older, and whose accounts are already set up for securities trading, subject to the bank’s terms. “For the first time in the banking system, Discount Bank will allow trading in digital currencies directly from the bank account in a simple and secure manner, without the need for complex dedicated digital wallets,” Avi Levi, CEO of Discount Group, said in the statement. “This is a first step toward establishing advanced technological infrastructure in the digital currency space and developing the bank’s capabilities in this area.” The rollout was led by Elad Fisher, head of the bank’s financial markets division. Coins will sit in bank-provided wallets built on infrastructure from Fireblocks. The bank said it may revisit transfers later. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Crypto Exchange Gemini Sells U.K. and EU Units to KAST for Under $10 Million Gemini Space Station has sold its already shuttered U.K. and European operations to Singapore stablecoin payments firm KAST for less than $10 million, according to CoinDesk reporting , as the exchange prepares to report third-quarter results after Thursday’s close. Gemini declined to comment. A spokesperson for KAST would not discuss the transaction, but said the company is actively looking at acquisitions as its revenue and footprint grow. Neither firm has issued a public confirmation of a sale, and no regulator has announced a change-of-control approval. The disposal, if confirmed, would close a retreat Gemini laid out in February. On Feb. 4, the Nasdaq-listed company, known as Gemini (GEMI), approved a plan to exit and wind down its operations in the United Kingdom, the European Union and other European jurisdictions, and Australia, as part of a broader effort to cut expenses and support a path to profitability. It said it would keep operating in the United States and Singapore. The plan included a reduction in force of up to 200 employees in Europe, the United States and Singapore, or about 25% of Gemini’s global workforce as of that date. The company estimated about $11 million in pre-tax restructuring charges, mostly in cash, and said it expected the wind-down to be substantially completed in the first half of 2026. Reuters reported the job cuts the same day. Co-founders Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss, who started Gemini in 2014 as a bitcoin exchange, told customers the firm would “double down on America” after foreign markets proved hard to win and stretched the company’s cost base. Gemini later told U.K., European Economic Area and Australian customers that their accounts would close on April 6, with withdrawals-only starting in early March. What would change hands in a sale is the leftover entities, staff and regulatory permissions from those already wound-down units, not Gemini’s core U.S. exchange. Buyers of shuttered crypto businesses often want the licenses more than the remaining operations. Any transfer of a licensed firm in the U.K. or the EU typically still requires a change-of-control review by local regulators before a new owner can run it. A payments firm with European ambitions KAST is a Singapore-based financial platform built on stablecoin rails. In March, it said it had raised $80 million in a Series A round co-led by QED Investors and Left Lane Capital. KAST provides dollar-denominated accounts, cross-border payments and cards that let consumers and businesses hold, move and spend stablecoins. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Rumble (RUM) Sells Two-Thirds of Its Bitcoin as AI Cloud Business Delivers First Profitable Quarter RUM Group, the parent of video platform Rumble, cut its bitcoin holdings by about two-thirds in the third quarter, the company disclosed Wednesday, as its newly acquired AI cloud business pushed it to its first profitable quarter on an adjusted basis. The Nasdaq-listed company held 94.68 bitcoin, valued at $7.9 million, as of Sept. 30. That compares with 293.14 bitcoin worth about $17.2 million at the end of June, according to its second-quarter results . That implies Rumble parted with roughly 198 bitcoin during the quarter, or about 68% of its stack. The company’s cash-flow statement shows a net sale of digital assets of about $15.3 million for the first nine months of 2026. In the same period a year earlier, it spent $19.1 million buying digital assets. Rumble did not explain the sales in its release, and it did not say what price it received. The balance sheet’s digital assets line, which the release does not break down, fell to $11.1 million from $18.5 million at the end of 2025. Rumble’s AI pivot takes over The bitcoin drawdown came in a quarter dominated by Quake AI, the cloud and AI infrastructure unit Rumble built around Northern Data, the German GPU operator it acquired in June. Revenue rose 290% from a year earlier to a record $96.6 million, beating the top of the company’s guidance range. Quake AI contributed $68.2 million of that, more than 70% of the total, in its first full quarter. The unit runs about 22,000 Nvidia GPUs, which the company said were about 85% utilized. Adjusted EBITDA came in at $4.4 million, the first positive result in company history. On a GAAP basis, RUM Group still lost $89.9 million, weighed down by $85.2 million in amortization and depreciation. Executives said on the call that about $39 million of that came from writing up the value of Northern Data’s assets in purchase accounting. “Quake AI is now the engine of our business,” CEO Chris Pavlovski said. “We have real assets running real AI workloads for real customers and generating real cash.” The video business itself grew more slowly. Rumble’s video segment brought in $28.4 million, up 15% year over year, and posted a $12.1 million adjusted EBITDA loss, wider than a year earlier, executives said on the call. Cash has been falling as well. RUM Group ended September with $134.4 million in cash and cash equivalents, down from $203.3 million at the end of June and $237.9 million at the end of 2025. The company raised its stake in Northern Data to about 98% during the quarter and expects to own all of it in early 2027. It also warned that part of the roughly 250 megawatts of unmonetized capacity it had targeted for 2027 may slip beyond that year due to market conditions. entertainment.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. It offers viewers a chance to see beyond the familiar celebrity image and learn more about the person behind it. entertainment.title: From Talking Drums to Tourism Diplomacy: How Nigeria Captured Attention at WTM London 2026
entertainment.description: With NTDA leading the national delegation, NTT Global Destinations mobilising international partnerships and diaspora networks, and NANTA representing Nigeria’s private tourism sector, the Nigeria Pavilion became a vibrant celebration of culture, community and tourism opportunities. For three exciting days, Nigeria brought its rhythm, culture, hospitality and entrepreneurial spirit to the global stage at World Travel Market (WTM) London 2026, held from 3 to 5 November at ExCeL London. Led by the Nigerian Tourism Development Authority (NTDA), under its Director General, Dr Olayiwola Awakan, the Nigeria Pavilion welcomed international visitors, tourism professionals, Nigerians and Africans living in the United Kingdom, and industry stakeholders who travelled from Nigeria. Supporting the national showcase was NTT Global Destinations (NGD), NTDA’s Strategic and Pavilion Implementation Partner, responsible for coordinating the exhibition’s planning, stakeholder engagement, international liaison and delivery. Together with the National Association of Nigeria Travel Agencies (NANTA) and diaspora media partners, Nigeria created an experience that extended beyond destination marketing. Day One: Nigeria Arrives in Colour and Rhythm The opening day brought the Nigeria Pavilion to life with traditional talking drums, cultural performances, networking and opportunities for visitors to experience Nigeria’s creative identity. From the energetic rhythms to conversations about Nigeria’s tourism offering, the pavilion quickly became a gathering point for visitors interested in discovering more about the country. Among the highlights was the opportunity to connect Nigerian culture with the global appeal of Nollywood, Afrobeats and contemporary African creativity. The Director General Who Stole the Show Perhaps one of the most memorable moments came when NTDA Director General, Dr Olayiwola Awakan, joined the traditional drummers and dancers in an energetic cultural performance. Rather than remaining a spectator, the DG became part of the attraction, embracing the rhythm and excitement of the Nigerian showcase. His performance drew attention and captured the spirit of the exhibition: a country confidently presenting its culture to the world. It was tourism diplomacy in its most authentic form, demonstrating that sometimes the most powerful way to promote a destination is simply to experience and celebrate it. Day Two: Tourism, Tradition and Private Sector Connections The second day combined cultural discovery with industry engagement, featuring a traditional palm wine experience, networking and interactions between Nigerian tourism stakeholders and international visitors. Held from October 16 to 23, 2026, the week-long festival took cocktail culture beyond borders, bringing together some of the most exciting talents and bar communities from Lagos, Accra, and Abidjan. At the heart of this year’s celebration was a powerful message: Africa’s cocktail industry thrives when creativity, culture, and expertise flow freely across borders. The celebrations took off on Sunday, October 18, as the Italian Trade Agency brought a touch of Italian sophistication to the festival with the Italian Cocktail Experience, an exclusive, invitation-only masterclass and Aperitivo Italiano held at Mr Panther, Victoria Island. The experience offered guests an opportunity to explore the artistry and traditions of Italian cocktail culture. Speaking at the event, Maurizio Ferri , Director of the Italian Trade Agency, highlighted the initiative’s goal of promoting Italian wines and spirits, featuring brands such as Campari, Aperol and Martini. The experience began with a masterclass hosted by Lara Rawa , founder of Lagos Cocktail Week, exploring five Italian classics: the Negroni, Americano, Bellini, Aperol Spritz and Garibaldi. Guests learned about the Italian aperitif tradition and how individual palates shape cocktail preferences. The evening continued with networking, Italian wine and cocktail tastings, and special guests, including Chef Gibbs and visiting bartenders from Abidjan and Ghana. With music by DJ Exclusive , the event combined cultural exchange, education and entertainment in celebration of Italian cocktail culture. One of the most exciting additions to this year’s festival was the debut of the Lagos Bar Show, a fresh take on the traditional bar hop that brought the spirit of Pan-African collaboration directly into some of Lagos’ most exciting bars. entertainment.title: Olamide’s Time & Space Is Almost Here! See the Cover Art & 10 Track List
entertainment.description: Olamide releases his new single Burukutu alongside his upcoming album Time & Space. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram If Olamide ‘s ‘ Burukutu ‘ has been on repeat, here’s something else to get into: the rapper has revealed the cover art and full tracklist for his upcoming album, Time & Space . Scheduled for release on November 16, 2026, under YBNL Nation and EMPIRE, the ten-track body of work follows a remarkable lineage of musical evolution from one of Africa’s most enduring creative forces. Adding a deeply personal touch to the rollout, Olamide revealed that he personally painted the striking cover art for the project. Olamide hand-painted the official artwork for his upcoming Time & Space, released via YBNL Nation and EMPIRE. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram Listeners have already caught an exciting glimpse of what to expect from the record through the release of the lead single, Burukutu . Named after the traditional, locally brewed fermented grain beverage, the track serves up rich street-level jubilation and celebratory culture, anchored by rhythmic cadences and unmistakable Yoruba-inflected delivery. The musical journey of Time & Space spans ten carefully curated titles designed to showcase his artistic range. The newly revealed tracklist opens with “ Elohim ” as the introductory piece, followed sequentially by “ Skoskola “, “ Say Less “, the lead anthem “ Burukutu “, and “ Alujon ” rounding out the first half. The second half picks up the tempo with “ Mbiri “, the collaborative track “ Jaiye ” featuring vocalist Fola , followed by “ Oshey “, “ Ring “, and the closing record “ Jogor “. Keeping features remarkably streamlined, the album highlights a targeted guest appearance from Nigerian singer Fola, allowing Olamide’s distinctive penmanship and vocal direction to take centre stage across the entire tracklist. The official 10-track tracklist for Olamide’s album Time & Space, featuring lead single Burukutu and a guest appearance by Fola. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram This forthcoming release arrives as the direct successor to his self-titled studio album, Olamidé , which dropped in June 2025 with a sprawling 17-track setup featuring heavyweights like Wizkid . Where that previous body of work leaned into massive collaborative constellations, Time & Space scales back into a more intimate, focused exploration of sound, anchored tightly by the creative vision of the YBNL boss himself. As November 16 approaches, anticipation continues to build across Lagos and beyond, cementing yet another brilliant chapter in Olamide’s legendary catalogue. entertainment.title: Celebrating 50 Years of Nourishment: Maltina Introduces Its New Look to Trade Partners
entertainment.description: Maltina has unveiled its refreshed visual identity at a trade launch event in Lagos, marking 50 years of nourishing Nigerian homes and introducing a new look for the iconic malt brand while retaining the taste and nutritional qualities consumers have come to love. First introduced as Maltona in 1976 and renamed Maltina in 1977, the brand has maintained a strong presence in Nigerian homes for over five decades. Its journey has been defined by a commitment to nourishment, including its introduction of multivitamin enrichment in 1993 and calcium fortification in 2009. The refreshed packaging features an enriched signature orange, gold accents and barley elements that reinforce Maltina’s malt credentials. The updated sunrays represent vitality and optimism, while the more prominent calcium coin highlights its nourishment proposition. The gold crown cork and the addition of ‘Since 1976’ further celebrate the brand’s heritage. She reassured consumers that while the brand’s visual identity has evolved, its familiar taste and nutritional credentials remain unchanged. entertainment.title: How to Style a Pink Buba With a Mini Skirt: Alex Unusual’s Loving Itohan Look
entertainment.description: Alex Unusual’s gold grillz, crystal floral choker, and cherub-accented sunglasses. Who says a buba has to be paired with a wrapper? Nigerian actress, media personality, and reality television star Asogwa Alexandra A —popularly known as Alex Unusua l—is giving us another way to wear the traditional Yoruba top, and her look for the premiere of Loving Itohan makes a strong case for pairing it with a mini skirt. The actress chose a bright fuchsia satin buba with wide half-sleeves, styling it with a fitted mini skirt made from emerald-green and magenta floral brocade damask . It’s an interesting way to rethink the familiar iro and bubacombination: keep the traditional top, swap the wrapper for a shorter skirt, and let the difference in fabric and colour give the outfit its character. The smooth finish of the pink satin against the patterned damask also shows how to wear two statement fabrics without making them compete . The trick is to give each piece a clear role, with the pink buba providing a bold block of colour and the brocade bringing in pattern and texture. Alex Unusual puts a modern spin on the Yoruba iro and buba with a satin top and brocade mini skirt. The mini skirt also gives the outfit a contemporary take on the Oleku silhouette, which traditionally pairs a loose or fitted buba with a wrapper tied above the knee. Alex’s version plays with that familiar proportion, using a fitted damask skirt in place of the wrapper. If you are wondering how to wear a buba and mini skirt without the proportions feeling off, the secret is balancing volume with structure. Because a traditional buba comes with a relaxed cut and wide sleeves, tucking it cleanly into a fitted, high-waisted mini skirt defines the waist and keeps the silhouette neat rather than boxy. Mixing textures intentionally helps too—pairing a plain silk, satin, or AsoOke top with a patterned damask, jacquard, or beaded mini skirt lets both pieces complement each other rather than clash. An oversized gold lip-shaped brooch secured one side, adding another detail to the headpiece. Using the same fabric for the skirt and gele also helped bring the different parts of the outfit together, while keeping the pink buba at the centre of the colour story.
