entertainment.description: Olumide Oworu has declared his candidacy for the Federal House of Representatives to represent Surulere Constituency 1 in 2027. Photo Credit: Olumide Oworu/Instagram Actor and media personality Olumide Oworu has declared his intention to contest for the Federal House of Representatives seat for Surulere Constituency 1 in the 2027 general elections. He will be running under the platform of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM). Olumide, who grew up in Surulere, Lagos, has a long-standing connection to the constituency. He began his acting career as a child, appearing in television productions such as Everyday People , before gaining wider recognition for his role in The Johnsons and other Nigerian film and television projects. This is his second attempt to enter legislative politics. In 2023, he declared his intention to contest for a seat in the Lagos State House of Assembly under the Labour Party. However, administrative challenges prevented his name from appearing on the final ballot. Olumide Oworu’s official campaign poster for the House of Representatives seat representing Surulere Constituency 1 under the Allied Peoples Movement. Photo Credit: Olumide Oworu/Instagram Reflecting on that experience in his candidacy announcement on Instagram, Olumide said the support he received from young people in Surulere had strengthened his belief in their readiness for more active participation in governance. “Despite the administrative hurdles that left our names off the final ballot, your resilience showed me that our vision was never a passing phase. Instead, it was the beginning of something much more significant,” he wrote. Explaining his decision to contest again, this time for a seat in the House of Representatives, he added: “We cannot afford to sit on the sidelines while our future is decided by a political class that won’t have to live with the consequences of today’s choices.” His campaign has highlighted issues including gaps in public services, community infrastructure and the participation of young Nigerians in policy decisions. Announcing his candidacy, he said he looked forward to continued support as he and his supporters worked towards what he described as a mission to “Reset Nigeria”. Olumide Oworu is contesting for a legislative seat in Surulere Constituency 1 under the APM platform. Photo Credit: Rema/Instagram Rema is getting ready to give fans a fresh body of music! The Nigerian singer has officially announced that his new seven-track EP, E-Mortal Boy ( EMB ), will be released next Friday, 20 November 2026. It’s been a little while since his last EP, so there’s plenty of reason for fans to be curious about what he has been working on. The 26-year-old Benin City star first introduced himself to listeners with his self-titled debut EP in 2019, released under Mavin Records and Jonzing World. Since then, he’s built an impressive catalogue, moving between different sounds while taking his music to audiences around the world. His 2022 debut album, Rave & Roses, marked a major turning point in his career, followed by the return to a more raw Afrobeats sound on the 2023 EP Ravage. In 2024, he switched things up again with HEIS , his high-intensity sophomore album, which earned him further international attention. Rema preparing for the release of his new EP E-Mortal Boy following his singles TEA and Oh No. Photo Credit: Rema/Instagram Now, Rema is opening another chapter with E-Mortal Boy (EMB). The project already has two singles to introduce its sound: “ Oh No ” and the fan-favourite “ TEA “. Both tracks give listeners an early taste of the music surrounding the new release, although Rema is keeping the rest of the project under wraps for now. The full tracklist and details of any featured artists have yet to be revealed. With seven tracks, E-Mortal Boy (EMB) will be Rema’s first EP since Ravage and his latest project following HEIS . The singer is set to release it on digital streaming platforms on 20 November, giving fans a new collection to get into as he continues to build on an already eventful musical journey. entertainment.title: Awar Odhiang Named Model of the Year at The Fashion Awards 2026
entertainment.description: Awar Odhiang featured in Vogue wearing a floral printed dress and sculpted oversized rose headpiece. Photo Credit: Awar Odhiang/Instagram Remember the model who turned the finale of Matthieu Blazy ‘s first Chanel show into one of the most talked-about runway moments of 2025? That was Awar Odhiang, and she has another major reason to celebrate. The South Sudanese-Canadian model has been named Model of the Year at The Fashion Awards 2026. The 25-year-old will receive the honour at London’s Royal Albert Hall on 30 November. Born in a refugee camp in Ethiopia and raised in Canada, Awar’s journey to the international fashion scene has taken her from being discovered in Alberta to walking some of the world’s biggest runways. She is now represented by major modelling agencies across London, Milan, Paris and New York. Awar Odhiang walking the red carpet at the 2026 Met Gala in New York City. Photo Credit: Awar Odhiang/Instagram Her runway résumé includes shows for Prada, Versace, Miu Miu, Saint Laurent and Jacquemus, but it was her appearance at Chanel’s Spring/Summer 2026 show in October 2025 that introduced her to an even wider audience. Closing Matthieu Blazy’s first collection for the fashion house, Awar wore the show’s bridal look, featuring an oversized white shirt and a voluminous, colourful feathered skirt. But it was what happened at the finale that captured everyone’s attention. As the models gathered for their final walk, Awar broke formation, smiling, clapping and twirling in her skirt. When Blazy appeared, she ran towards him and embraced him. The spontaneous moment quickly went viral, with fashion fans celebrating the joy she brought to the runway. It was also a historic appearance: Awar became only the third Black woman to close a Chanel show in the house’s 115-year history, after Alek Wek and Adut Akech. Model of the Year 2026 winner Awar Odhiang backstage at the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show. Photo Credit: Awar Odhiang/Instagram Since then, her career has continued to gather pace. Awar has appeared on eight international magazine covers this year and fronted campaigns for Chanel, Chloé, Louis Vuitton, Saint Laurent, Loro Piana and H&M. She has also used her growing platform to speak up for greater representation and inclusion of Black models in the luxury fashion industry. Awar Odhiang in Daniel Roseberry’s Schiaparelli Spring 2026 Haute Couture collection in Paris. Photo Credit: Awar Odhiang/Instagram Her Model of the Year recognition celebrates a remarkable year of runway, editorial and campaign work, as well as the influence she continues to have beyond the catwalk. On 30 November, she’ll take that recognition to the Royal Albert Hall, adding another milestone to a career that is still unfolding. entertainment.title: Ayra Starr Joins Coachella 2027 Lineup Alongside SZA, Dua Lipa & More
entertainment.description: Ayra Starr returns with her third studio album, Starrgirl. Ayra Starr is taking her global run to another big stage! The Nigerian singer has been named among the performers at Coachella 2027, adding another major festival appearance to her growing list of international milestones. The Beninese-born singer, who rose to prominence as one of Afrobeats’ leading voices after joining Mavin Records, is set to perform on both weekends of the festival, Sunday, April 11, and Sunday, April 18, 2027. Coachella will take place at the Empire Polo Club in Indio, California. It’s been a big year for Ayra, with her third studio album, Starrgirl, adding to an already exciting run. Fans heading to the festival can look forward to hearing songs from the project, including “ Tornado ” and “ Midnight in New York “, as well as her collaboration “ Gimme Dat “. There’s also room for crowd favourites such as “ Rush “, “ Commas ” and “ Heaven Baby “. Ayra shares the Sunday bill with headliner SZA , alongside Victoria Monét , Jorja Smith , Becky G and Don Toliver . The wider festival, running from April 9 to 11 and April 16 to 18, will also feature headliners Dua Lipa and Tame Impala , with Madonna set for a special appearance in the dance tent. Her Coachella booking follows another major moment in London, where she performed at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium as part of the NFL International Games halftime show, becoming the first African artist to headline the show. And there’s even more for fans to look forward to. Ayra has announced her 20-city Starrgirl World Tour , which will take her across Europe and North America in early 2027 before she heads to the California desert for Coachella. sports.title: Florida turns recruiting momentum into commitment from 2027 OT Moreno Fisher
sports.description: Florida has landed one of the fastest-rising offensive linemen in the 2027 class. Moreno Fisher , a 6-foot-7, 270-pound offensive tackle out of Cornelius (N.C.) Hough , has committed to Jon Sumrall and the Gators following his official visit to Gainesville. The former Virginia commit saw his recruitment take off this fall. Auburn , Florida and Florida State were among the major programs to extend offers after Fisher reopened his recruitment. But Florida made its move early, and the Gators never let up. Fisher first visited Gainesville in September for the Ole Miss game. That trip gave Florida momentum, and offensive line coach Phil Trautwein continued building on it. Now the Gators have landed another offensive lineman for their 2027 recruiting class. “The experience and the whole environment of that game was something crazy,” Fisher previously told Rivals. “It was a daytime game, and it was still packed out. No open seats in the crowd. It was a great experience, honestly.” That first visit helped Fisher see Florida differently. The atmosphere impressed him, but the coaching staff ultimately helped separate the Gators from the competition. Trautwein made Fisher a priority from the moment Florida offered. The Gators’ offensive line coach stayed in regular contact, explained his vision for Fisher’s development and established a strong relationship with the North Carolina standout. “I like Coach Trautwein a lot. He has coached some great offensive linemen. Since offering me, he has recruited me hard. He is a top coach.” Sumrall also made a strong impression. Fisher followed Florida’s progress throughout the season and liked how the Gators responded to adversity. “Coach Sumrall has done a great job,” Fisher said. “They have a great atmosphere at Florida. The crowd is great. It is a top SEC school and the coaches have them playing well.” Florida’s staff continued making Fisher feel wanted after his September visit. Sumrall, Trautwein and other staff members maintained weekly communication, and the Gators made an in-person stop to see Fisher ahead of his official visit. That consistent attention mattered. “Honestly, it’s because of how they make me feel, coming from a coaching staff standpoint and a player standpoint,” Fisher said. “They make me feel like a priority.” Fisher also took notice of the direction of the program. “Then the way they carry themselves so far this season, bouncing back from losses, responding. It’s all just right in front of me. I like what they are about.” By the time Fisher returned to Gainesville for his official visit, Florida had established itself as the program to beat. The Gators used that opportunity to finish the job. Fisher’s commitment gives Florida a massive offensive tackle prospect with considerable upside. At 6-foot-7 and 270 pounds, he brings the length and frame that college programs covet at the position.

sports.title: Real Madrid complete their first signing of the 2027/28 season – report
sports.description: Real Madrid complete their first signing of the 2027/28 season – report According to MARCA , Real Madrid have completed an agreement to sign Ghanaian midfielder Latif Issman from UD Logrones, with the youngster set to join Castilla next summer. The deal was finalised today, making the 20-year-old the club’s first acquisition for the 2027-28 campaign. Real Madrid tracking Issman since the summer Issman, who is represented by MS Sports, has been on Real Madrid’s radar since the summer. The Spanish capital club made an attempt to sign him towards the end of the summer window, but were unable to get the deal across the line. However, having missed out on his signing in the summer, Los Blancos stepped up their efforts in recent weeks and have now been successful in reaching an agreement with UD Logrones. The two clubs already have a working relationship, having negotiated the transfer of Manex Rezola to Valdebebas last winter. Issman’s current contract with UD Logrones runs until June 30, 2027, meaning his move to Real Madrid will coincide with the end of his existing deal. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Rising Football Pros (@risingfootballpros_gh) Previous reports suggested that the midfielder had a release clause worth €300,000 in his contract with Logrones. For now, it is unclear if Real Madrid have paid that sum or negotiated a lower fee, or will be signing Issman for free. Who is Latif Issman? Born on November 1, 2006, Issman began his development at SD Logrones before moving to UD Logrones at youth level. He made the step up to the senior squad in July 2025 and gradually established himself as an important part of the team. Unai Mendia gave him playing time in all four matches during the promotion play-offs. His involvement increased further following the club’s promotion to RFEF Primera Federacion , where he has featured in ten games, even registering one assist. The 20-year-old Ghanaian talent also has one appearance in the Copa del Rey this season. Latif Issman will be Real Madrid’s first signing for next summer. (Photo by Gonzalo Arroyo Moreno/Getty Images) As per the report, Real Madrid’s interest is understood to have been driven by Issman’s physical presence and ability to break opposition lines. The midfielder attracted offers from several clubs, but the Merengues moved decisively to secure his signature. He is viewed as a potential long-term option in the No. 8 role at Valdebebas. His ability to provide balance in a double pivot, while also making forward runs and contributing to attacks, makes him an appealing profile for Castilla. With his signing for Real Madrid now completed, the next step for Issman will be adapting to the demands of the club’s reserve team when he arrives next summer.

sports.title: Arsenal hold Barca to women's Champions League draw
sports.description: Barcelona's Norwegian forward Caroline Graham Hansen pulled the holders level with Arsenal before the hour mark (MANAURE QUINTERO) Arsenal earned an impressive 1-1 draw at women's Champions League holders Barcelona on Thursday in a league phase clash between two of the competition's heavyweights. Caroline Graham Hansen secured four-time champions Barca, who have reached the final six seasons running, a point after Frida Maanum fired visitors Arsenal into a surprise lead at Camp Nou. The Gunners beat Barcelona in the 2025 final in Lisbon in the teams' last meeting and, despite Renee Slegers's team's domestic struggles, dug deep to deliver on the big stage again. The draw leaves Barca, second, level on 10 points with leaders Lyon after four matches, while the Londoners are fourth, level on eight points with third-place Bayern Munich and Chelsea. Two-time winners Arsenal had a golden opportunity in the opening stages when Caitlin Foord broke into the box but Irene Paredes blocked brilliantly. The rebound fell to Alessia Russo, who headed against the post from point-blank range, but appeared to be offside. Barcelona took control after that, with Graham Hansen and Sydney Schertenleib forcing Arsenal's Misa Rodriguez into two saves at her near post. The visitors, who are languishing in sixth in the English top flight, rode out the barrage and nosed ahead through Maanum after 22 minutes. Barcelona goalkeeper Cata Coll saved well from Foord but Norwegian midfielder Maanum reacted quickest to latch on to the rebound and slot home. Graham Hansen ran Arsenal left-back Taylor Hinds ragged but Barca could not break through before the interval. Claudia Pina fired narrowly wide after a burst inside from the left and Paredes looped a header over the crossbar. Graham Hansen's header clipped the post just before the break as Pere Romeu's Barca went in frustrated, but the Norwegian winger pulled them level before the hour mark. Esmee Brugts found Graham Hansen in the box and she cut inside Steph Catley and whipped a strike into the top left corner. Russo might have put Arsenal back in front but hammered over when well placed after being teed up by substitute Olivia Smith. Arsenal resisted Barcelona pressure in the final stages to end the hosts' 100 percent start to the competition. rbs/ea

sports.title: Providence to host women's basketball franchise in spring 2027
sports.description: PROVIDENCE — Women's professional basketball is coming to Amica Mutual Pavilion beginning in May. That's when the UpShot League will debut downtown, with Providence officially awarded an expansion franchise at a Thursday morning press conference in the venue's front lobby. Managing partner Mark Walsh said the Providence franchise will play its home opener May 13, part of a 28-game schedule that will run through the spring and summer. The league debuted in 2026 with four teams and is in the process of adding new markets ahead of its 2027 return. More: Rhode Island’s new UFL team has a name. Meet the Breakers "This is your team," Walsh said. "We want this to be your team. We are not asking for any money from the community — we are asking you for support." Gov. Dan McKee, Providence Mayor Brett Smiley and House Speaker Joseph Shekarchi were among the state political delegation gathered Thursday. They joined several executives from the Rhode Island Convention Center — CEO Dan McConaghy, chairman Ernest Almonte and general manager Larry Lepore. The state's basketball community was represented by former Providence College basketball star Ernie DiGregorio, former Johnston High and Friars standout Chelsea Marandola and former Providence players Harold Starks and Quinton Burton. "Providence is a great basketball city and it just became greater because of today's announcement," Smiley said. Walsh attempted to position the Providence franchise as a professional replacement for the Connecticut Sun, which played its last WNBA game 48 days ago and will relocate to Houston. Providence was among the cities that made both a presentation and formal offer to that team's owners in an attempt to keep them in the region. Discussions soon pivoted to the UpShot delegation while attempting to fill more dates downtown outside the traditional fall and winter schedules played by the Providence College men and Providence Bruins. "This team will give women a great opportunity to continue improving their basketball skills and to grow within the sport," Almonte said. "It will give players, coaches and referees a stage to showcase their talents and potentially move up to the WNBA." McKee attended the press conference with his daughter, Kara, a former player in their hometown of Cumberland. She was part of the first all-girls league in their community and developed into a state champion prior to her entry into high school. McKee asked her to recruit five classmates while starting their first team. That number eventually grew to more than 100 girls participating. "Full circle to be standing here at the AMP," McKee said. "A win for women's sports, a win for our capital city and a win for Rhode Island. Welcome." What is the UpShot League? The UpShot League was founded by Florida-based Zawyer Sports & Entertainment in January 2025. Investors include women's basketball greats Cheryl Miller, Ann Meyers Drysdale and Tamika Catchings and former Florida standout Patric Young. Jacksonville

sports.description: EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks . One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished. Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season. “One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity,” sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said. After his team’s 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward. I think that’s challenging, too, especially when you’re young, to not lose a little bit of gusto and not lose a little bit of belief.” Oregon linebacker Devon Jackson (#9) drops UCLA running back Wayne Knight (#3) for no gain as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. sports.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
sports.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. sports.title: Oregon has 3 quarterbacks who could start Saturday. Illinois has a freshman who's never started before
sports.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. sports.title: The Risk the Tigers Are Taking on Emilio Pagan
sports.description: The Detroit Tigers have agreed to a one-year deal worth $11 million with relief pitcher Emilio Pagan, a deal the New York Post first reported . Pagan is 35 and turns 36 during the 2027 MLB season, and he is the favorite to take over the ninth inning in Detroit after the Tigers declined their 2027 club option on Kenley Jansen . Pagan declined a $10 million player option with the Cincinnati Reds for the 2027 season. The move got him at least $1 million more than the option he turned down. Addressing the bullpen was a good thing for Scott Harris. Whether Detroit picked the right arm to do it is the question. Cincinnati Reds pitcher Emilio Pagán (15) cheers after striking out Tommy White for the final out of the ninth inning of the MLB Interleague game between the Cincinnati Reds and the Athletics at Great American Ball Park in downtown Cincinnati on Wednesday, Aug. 5, 2026. The Reds won the second game of the series, 3-2. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Emilio Pagan missed 47 games with a hamstring strain last season Even though the Tigers appear to have found their closer for the 2027 MLB season, Pagan missed 47 games during the 2026 MLB season with Cincinnati because of a left hamstring strain. He was carted off the field after a single pitch on May 5 , and the Reds did not have him back on the active roster until June 30 . Pagan pitched in 45 games for Cincinnati last season. His record was 5-1 with a 3.38 ERA . In 42.2 innings pitched, he gave up 33 hits and 16 runs, walked 11 batters and struck out 45. His WHIP was 1.03, and he recorded 25 saves on 28 attempts. The case for the signing is in what he did after he got healthy. From July 1 on, Pagan put up a 1.88 ERA over his final 30 appearances and converted every one of his 19 save chances. Detroit is not paying for the version of Pagan who opened the season. It is paying for the one who closed it. The Reds already have a name to replace him Moving off of Pagan could be a good thing for Cincinnati. The Yahoo Sports piece on his departure floated Brock Burke, who is 30, as the arm the Reds could lean on in a similar role in 2027. That is five years younger than the pitcher Detroit just committed to, and Burke posted a 2.30 ERA with 74 strikeouts after Cincinnati acquired him from the Los Angeles Angels last offseason. Tigers bullpen can’t afford to have Pagan injured in 2027 One of the major issues with Detroit during the 2026 MLB season was its bullpen, and the damage was concentrated exactly where Pagan is being asked to work. Detroit relievers posted a 9.21 ERA in high-leverage situations in 2026, which ranked 30th in baseball. Harris has said he wants swing-and-miss stuff and a veteran presence added to that group this winter, and Pagan checks both boxes . The problem is what happens if the hamstring goes again. sports.title: Nelly Korda shoots bogey-free 63 in return at The Annika
sports.description: Nelly Korda opened The Annika with a bogey-free 7-under 63 on Thursday at Pelican Golf Club. It was her first start since the Solheim Cup in mid-September. The world No. 1 made five birdies on the front nine to turn in 30. She added birdies at Nos. 14 and 17 on the way in and finished two shots behind playing partner Hye-Jin Choi, who shot 61 to take the early lead. Korda skipped the LPGA’s four-event Asia swing. She said she was burned out when the Solheim Cup matches ended in the Netherlands, and decided to take a five-day vacation in Greece. After that, she recharged at home. Korda said her favorite things during the break were cooking, sleeping in her own bed and going to the gym. "Just getting in a routine of being like a normal kind of human being," she said. "I think that's what reenergizes my batteries the most." Korda, 28, has dealt with neck problems in recent seasons and is comfortable trimming her schedule. “My body just can’t do that,” she said of the 30-event seasons some rookies play. “Once I start to feel something I just have to take that break.” She said her familiarity with Jason McDede, her caddie of eight years, gave her comfort coming back. “He knows exactly what to say, and we switch right back into that routine,” she said. Additionally, her putting coach, David Angelotti, is with her this week. Korda said their work did not change during the break and that she likes to keep things simple in her camp. “I don’t want to know all the numbers,” she said. “I just want to know a few simple keys.” Korda's return comes at a consequential time. She clinched her second Rolex Player of the Year award last week , which gave her 26 of the 27 points needed for the LPGA Hall of Fame. A win this week or at next week’s CME Group Tour Championship would earn her the last point. She would be the third-youngest player to enter the LPGA’s Hall of Fame , behind Lydia Ko and Inbee Park. Korda has won four times in 2026, including the Chevron Championship and the U.S. Women’s Open. She has good memories at the Annika, having won it three times, but commented that the Hall of Fame is not on her mind. “Is the Hall of Fame something I’m really looking at? Not at all,” she said. “I mean, I’m just focusing on being competitive and trying to give it my all. ... After that, everything else is out of my control." sports.title: LHSAA State Volleyball roundup: Here are the 337-area teams advancing to semifinals
sports.description: Eight girls volleyball teams hailing from Lafayette Parish and the surrounding area punched their tickets to the 2026 Sugar Bowl LHSAA State Volleyball Tournament . After months of matches and countless volleys, St. Thomas More, Iota, Teurlings Catholic, Lafayette Christian, Northside Christian, Catholic-N.I., Westminster Christian-Opelousas and Episcopal of Acadiana made it to the big stage inside the Cajundome, all with the hope of snagging a state title and bringing hardware back to their respective communities. All eight area teams kicked off the quarterfinals on Thursday, Nov. 12, and halfway through Day 1, three teams have earned a spot in Friday’s semifinals round. Here’s a roundup of the 337-area teams whose postseason dreams remain alive. ESA Falcons take down fellow 337 foe In one of the opening games of the quarterfinals, Episcopal of Acadiana and Northside Christian faced off in a battle of 337 teams in Division V. The Falcons started the first set slow but quickly found their rhythm to go on to sweep the Warriors 3-0. The key was ESA’s one-two punch at the outside hitter position. “Lauren (Conroy) has been a huge contributor to our offense all season long. We got the bang-bang with both of our outside hitters, which is really fun to watch,” ESA coach Sara Robichaux said. “We’ve got a couple of other key players who have been huge in playing their role to help our outside hitters do what they do.” Conroy led the Falcons with a game-high 14 kills, and senior outside hitter Avery Monica followed her with nine kills. Leading Northside Christian in defeat senior middle hitter Khyra Abshire with 10 kills. ESA will face Riverside Academy in the semifinals. WCA-Opelousas, LCA get over quarterfinals hump For WCA-Opelousas and LCA, the quarterfinals round carried some bitterness after seeing their seasons end in this round last year. That wasn't the case this time around. The Crusaders took on First Baptist Christian in DV and they dominated in all three sets to sweep the Eagles 3-0. Leading the charge was Londyn Pickney with nine kills and two blocks. “It means a lot for us to win today since last year we had unfortunately came up short,” Pickney said. “So this year, we really wanted to prioritize our energy, no matter who we play. Our energy wins games.” Over in DIV, LCA took on a higher-seeded Isidore Newman squad. The Knights got to taste just how sweet revenge is as they beat the Greenies 3-0. Last year it was the Greenies who swept them in this same round. “Usually our road to the finals goes through either Newman or John Curtis,” LCA coach Bryan Barrett said. “I think our experience this year was the difference. We had seniors but a lot of those seniors didn’t play a ton. But this crew came back from last year and I’ve only got one senior.” The Knights' lone senior, outside hitter Demi Barrett, was nearly unstoppable, racking up a game-high 15 kills. sports.title: Who's on second? Detroit Tigers have plethora of options for 2027
sports.description: Who will start at second base for the Detroit Tigers in 2027? “I think we have a number of really good options,” Tigers president of baseball operations Scott Harris said at the GM meetings in Las Vegas on Tuesday, Nov. 10. Hao-Yu Lee, who made his MLB debut in 2026, is in a fantastic position. “He's got a great shot to be our second baseman,” Harris said. Lee started 53 games at second and 32 at third in 2026, which was an up-and-down season for him. Or rather, it was down, then up. When Lee made his big-league debut, he was overmatched, hitting .205 in 83 at-bats over 32 games. “So he came up, struggled, sent him down to work on some adjustments,” Harris said. Lee was sent down on June 2. After spending about two weeks at Triple-A Toledo, he returned to Detroit and was fantastic, hitting .283 with eight home runs and 16 doubles in 82 games for an .802 OPS. “He came back, and he just absolutely raked the rest of the summer,” Harris said. Lee could also play third base. “We've asked him to do a couple different things,” Tigers manager A.J. Hinch said of Lee during the season. “He's made progress at both positions.” Hinch said he has seen Lee improve. “The turn of the double play has gotten better,” Hinch said. “I have a ton of confidence in him.” But Lee is not a finished product. “I think the eye test tells me he's a really good defender who has to work on the consistency of his fundamentals to be able to be a better overall player,” Hinch said. While Lee appears to be the most obvious option at second, the Tigers have several other options, including John Peck, Kevin McGonigle, Zach McKinstry, Javier Báez and Max Anderson, who won a minor league Gold Glove at second base. “John Peck − really good opportunity to build on the experience that he had this year,” Harris said, running through options at second. “Obviously, we have Kevin. Obviously, we have Zach. Obviously, we have Javy. We have a number of really good options. Max Anderson is forcing his way into the conversation now. I'm sure I missed some guys who play second base. We're waiting to build the whole team and then make that decision.” It was interesting that Harris mentioned McGonigle at second. Because Hinch mentioned that McGonigle could play second (as well as short or third) during the season. It's just based on how the rest of the infield is configured. "I'm not saying he's going to be a second baseman, but he did it a little bit in the fall league [in 2025],” Hinch said of McGonigle. "We haven't asked him to do it this year with Gleyber [Torres] being here. It hasn't made a ton of sense to put any time there, but I think everything's open depending on how the team's built.” Another option: Anderson. Harris has said that he expects Anderson to be in Detroit at some point in 2027. To be clear, the organization has not made a definitive decision at second. sports.description: Free agent outfielder Seiya Suzuki The Boston Red Sox ranked 26th in home runs and 18th in OPS last season, and they are reportedly focused on improving their offense this winter. This is a weak free-agent class and Seiya Suzuki is one of the best available hitters. The team has "checked in on" him, according to The Boston Globe's Alex Speier. "The Sox are looking to add righthanded thump to take advantage of Fenway — the team, according to major league sources, also has checked in on free agent outfielder Seiya Suzuki," wrote Speier. Suzuki has a .823 career OPS and hit 26 home runs for the Chicago Cubs last season. However, the biggest development for Suzuki was the fact that he was actually a good defender. His defense had been an issue in the big leagues, but he was a Gold Glove finalist in right field last season. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? He could bang a ton of balls off the Green Monster and infuse the Red Sox lineup with some much-needed power from the right side. His fit on the team would be odd, but that could change if the Red Sox clear the outfield logjam by getting rid of Jarren Duran and Masataka Yoshida. The Red Sox would have Roman Anthony, Ceddanne Rafaela, Wilyer Abreu and Suzuki. It would be a lot easier to navigate at-bats for those four than it is currently with Anthony, Duran, Yoshida, Abreu and Rafaela. Suzuki would either have to be a full-time designated hitter or learn to play left field. Abreu is a Gold Glover in right field, and the Red Sox are not going to remove him. technology.title: Software Samaritan revamps borked Indian certs to block smart TV ads
technology.description: eMudhra's private key exposure has been a security disaster, but it also means that you can block those annoying ads on smart TVs if you’re so inclined. Luckily for those with some know-how and a hatred of smart TV ads, Czech software developer Daniel Vrátil has done the work for you and published his project on GitHub for anyone who wants to take a stab at it - and do the legwork to add support for their own ad-riddled television. Vrátil said he’d been blocking ads on his Samsung smart TV using a Pi-hole (DNS-based ad-blocking software that can run on a Raspberry Pi, for those unfamiliar), but right around the time the eMudhra certificate leak mess unfolded, he had messed something up while tinkering with his home lab and the ads were back. First, here's a bit of background on the eMudhra mess. The company, based in India, operated a publicly trusted HTTPS certificate authority and says it has issued more than 60 million digital certificates. As we learned last month , eMudhra wasn't doing its best to keep its cryptographic keys safe: Eight intermediate CA private keys were found to be absurdly weak, with one being the number four and the others consisting of two- or three-digit numbers that could be guessed with little effort. eMudhra has since left the CA racket , saying that it wasn’t a big deal to it since issuing certs was a small part of its business. The company has blamed a bad software script put in place to generate keys that its hardware couldn’t handle as the root of the issue. What all that means, in a practical sense, is that anyone could forge an eMudhra certificate to spoof a website and do something malicious. It also means that security researchers who were able to get their hands on devices that still trust eMudhra certificates could have a field day learning how their communications work, which is exactly what Vrátil took advantage of. eMudhra private keys were added to the open source mitmproxy service - a fully interactive HTTPS proxy that can be used for good or bad - shortly after they were exposed. Pair that with a 2022 Samsung smart TV that still trusts the compromised eMudhra certificates, and you have a way to inspect its HTTPS traffic and redirect selected requests to a server of your choosing. By Vrátil’s account, swapping out annoying ads for pictures of his family on his TV’s main screen was a pretty simple task. “Luckily for me, Samsung did not yet release an update for my TV that would revoke the certificate,” Vrátil explained in his writeup. “This allowed me to route all traffic from the TV through mitmproxy and get a list of all the domains and endpoints that my TV talks to, but also see the structure of the requests and response payloads.” The advertising traffic flow was pretty basic, it turns out: Activity on the TV is relayed to an ad server, which serves up ads on the home screen based on a JSON response. science.title: 'Warhammer Survivors' is the perfect gateway into the 40K universe
science.description: We've had no shortage of great Warhammer 40K games lately, but most aren't exactly aimed at the casual crowd. Warhammer Survivors changes that, finally providing curious gamers with an easy entry point into the grim darkness of the 41st millennium. Developed by Auroch Digital (in collaboration with Vampire Survivors' Poncle), this new spin on the survivors-like roguelite subgenre mixes the sci-fi 40,000 setting with the pure fantasy Age of Sigmar universe. This means heroes and enemies from all over the Warhammer mythos meet together in a bite-sized game that anyone can figure out and enjoy in less than five minutes. When you look at the alternatives, that's a remarkable achievement for a franchise that's notoriously hard (and often expensive) to get into . Warhammer Survivors isn't bogged down by dense lore, involved mechanics, or massive campaign playthroughs. It's more of an "inspired by" effort that gives casuals a small taste of the series' iconic characters — including Boltgun 's Malum Caedo — and factions like the terrifying Tyranids, the raucous Orks, and the foul forces of Chaos. All of 40K's (and Age of Sigmar's) recognizable elements are on display, but they serve more as flavoring sprinkled on top of Vampire Survivors' successful formula. If you're new to the Survivors-like subgenre, it's a unique gaming experience. You battle an endless onslaught of enemies that slowly march towards you, with your character passively attacking automatically. You only need to move them around sprawling arenas and select level-up upgrades and items after collecting enough gems (skulls in this case). The moment-to-moment gameplay is as simple as it can get outside of walking sims and interactive "experiences," but there's a deceiving depth to item synergies and how to correctly "build" characters to endure all the carnage. Unlike Poncle's original game, Warhammer Survivors struggles a bit to get going. The early hours are sluggish until you unlock certain meta upgrades, but its still got that Vampire Survivors magic at its core. As far as "podcast/gym games" go, this is a perfect fit. There's just enough going on to keep one's brain engaged, but minimal inputs and a tight overarching design lead to a rhythm that's easy to get into without using much brainpower. It's oddly satisfying to weave through enemies and level up your firepower, watching a single Astra Militarum grunt grow into a full Lasgun-spamming, chainsword-wielding wrecking ball. Achievement and unlock hunters will find enough to bite into here, too. It's unclear if the devs will continue to add more Warhammer 40K and Age of Sigmar deep cuts to this game via DLCs and free updates, but those universes have daunting depths to explore. This really could become a gateway game for future 40K fans: by the time they realize they're hooked, they'll already have 2000 pts of space marines painted and ready to play. science.title: Dark matter breakthrough coming? Euclid space telescope unveils its 1st look into the dark universe (video)
science.description: null On Thursday (Nov. 12), the Euclid space telescope released its first major batch of data, capturing the light of more than a billion objects over an area of sky as big as 9,500 full moons. The data release lays the foundation for one of the largest-ever 3D maps of the cosmos and many groundbreaking discoveries about the nature of dark energy and dark matter. The European Space Agency 's (ESA) Euclid space telescope has been called the "Dark Universe Detective" because of its capability to investigate the dual mysteries of dark matter , the universe's most mysterious stuff, and dark energy , the force accelerating the expansion of the universe. Collectively, these cosmic elements are sometimes referred to as the dark universe. The new data release, designated DR1-Foundation, was built from 13 months of observations and is accompanied by a multitude of images, including large sky mosaics. It marks the first major release of mission data since Euclid launched in mid-2023 . The core of the Messier 81 galaxy group as seen by Euclid. (Image credit: ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin) "These are far more than beautiful pictures; today marks a scientific milestone in our study of the cosmos," ESA's Director of Science, Carole Mundell said in a statement . "This major Euclid data release represents the largest space-based survey of its kind, laying the foundation of future discovery in a new regime for astronomy and demonstrating the excellence of European technology, science and international collaboration." What's in the Euclid release The ESA put into raw numbers the sheer number of celestial objects viewed by the Dark Universe Detective and contained in DR1-Foundation. That includes light spectra from 160 million sources, over 900 million galaxies, and 60 million candidates for quasars , regions of space dominated by feeding supermassive black holes . "This is a change in scale from Euclid's previous releases, which included a few days of observations over around 60 degrees squared of sky," ESA's Euclid project scientist Valeria Pettorino said. "We're now releasing more than a year of data covering a significantly larger area. This unlocks groundbreaking science." NGC 1291, a striking ring galaxy lying around 33 million light-years away from us, as seen by Euclid. (Image credit: ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. Bertin) Euclid can see such a vast number of cosmic objects thanks to the fact that its space-based position helps it avoid interference caused by Earth's atmosphere. This includes clusters of galaxies and even larger superclusters. science.title: I used the Vaonis Vespera 3 for weeks and here’s who I would recommend it to — full review
science.description: null I’ve spent a lot of time with smart telescopes , from relatively inexpensive Seestar models to the original Vaonis Vespera and the Vespera Pro . They all promise essentially the same thing — you put a telescope outside at night, choose something interesting on your smartphone and let the technology take care of the rest. The Vaonis Vespera 3 does that exceptionally well, but after spending several nights with it, I’m convinced it’s designed for a rather different kind of buyer. The telescope’s optical arm folds into its curved body when switched off. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) At $2,490/£2,199, this is hardly an impulse purchase for the beginner who’s curious about astronomy – you could buy several perfectly capable smart telescopes for the same money. Yet I found myself increasingly impressed by what the Vespera 3 could achieve, particularly when I returned to the same object over several nights. The images were sharp, the colors were excellent and I almost never had to think about the battery. The Vespera III weighs 13 lbs (6 kg) including the tripod. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) That doesn’t mean the experience was flawless. I sometimes spent longer than I’d have liked waiting for the telescope to get ready, but once it began photographing the sky, the Vespera 3 reminded me why I love smart telescopes so much. Why I kept returning to the same objects over several nights The Vespera 3 uses a Sony IMX585 sensor to produce 8.3MP images. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) One of my favorite things about smart telescopes is watching a photograph develop as more light is collected. What begins as a fairly ordinary patch of stars gradually becomes something much more interesting. First a faint cloud of gas appears, then more structure emerges, and eventually you have an image that, only a few short years ago, would have been difficult to capture without specialist equipment. With the Vespera 3, I spent several nights photographing the Pleiades (M45), the famous star cluster in Taurus. The Pleiades make an excellent subject for testing a telescope because the stars are bright, but the surrounding nebulosity is much harder to capture convincingly. The Singularity app used to control Vespera 3 stacks each image as it goes, but keeps them in sight as an optional time-lapse, so you can see exactly why you’re spending so much time on one object. Even better, the Vespera 3’s PerseverENS feature lets you add data to an existing observation over multiple nights (it’s actually called multi-night observation in the app). Instead of having to call it a night or start again every time the weather interrupts an imaging session, you can return to a target and continue building the image over weeks — or years. This is excellent for faint nebulas, but also for anyone who lives somewhere with unpredictable weather. science.title: Satellite snaps rare birds-eye view of the ISS | Space photo of the day for Nov. 12, 2026
science.description: null A satellite looks down at the International Space Station in orbit. (Image credit: HEO) A commercial satellite has spotted the International Space Station (ISS), giving us a unique view of the orbiting lab from above. What is it? Most of the time, when we see the ISS, it is from down here on Earth or from the viewpoint of the astronauts onboard, peering out the windows at the station's limbs, solar arrays and instruments. But in this snapshot, which was posted on X on Nov. 9 by the Australian company HEO, we can see the station stretched out in all its glory. HEO specializes in using satellites in low Earth orbit to capture images of other spacecraft, though longer-term the company aims to capture observations far out into the solar system. HEO doesn't build the satellites that take these photos; rather, the company's software tasks the spacecraft to image targets as they come into range. This great photo of the ISS from above, for example, was taken by a satellite operated by BlackSky, a Virginia-based company that holds a non-Earth imaging agreement with HEO . So far, HEO and its partners have captured imagery of a variety of spacecraft in orbit, including the ISS, China's Tiangong space station and the European Space Agency's ERS-2 satellite (while it was hurtling back to Earth in 2024). Why is it incredible? While it might seem that satellites are just hovering above Earth, the space station and other spacecraft in LEO are hurtling through space at roughly 17,500 mph (28,160 kph), hundreds of miles above our planet's surface. A snapshot of a satellite from above is therefore far from mundane. Rather, it requires incredible coordination and technical skill; satellite operators must know precisely when their target will present itself, and their equipment must be capable of getting the shot.

Bertin, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO The European Space Agency has just released a vast batch of observations of the sky captured by the Euclid space telescope. Launched in 2023, the telescope is currently on a six-year mission to image about one-third of the sky to build the most detailed 3D map of the cosmos ever created . The latest observations – catchily titled DR1-Foundation – cover an area of the sky as big as 9500 full moons. The collection includes 900 million galaxies. The mosaic of 740 images at the top of the article, collected in autumn 2024 and spring 2025, covers 367 square degrees of the northern sky. At full resolution, this snapshot runs to 500 gigapixels. Bertin, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO The image above shows Messier 81 in greater detail, along with part of the M81 group of galaxies that also bears its name – an honour bestowed on it as the largest galaxy of the bunch. To the lower left is the smaller galaxy NGC 3077, and the patches of wispy blue cloud throughout the images are galactic cirrus, which are actually in the foreground and part of our own home galaxy. ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, image processing by J.-C. Cuillandre and E. science.title: The 'eclipse of the century' will plunge these 8 wonders of the Roman Empire into darkness on Aug. 2, 2027
science.description: null Ancient Egyptian temples will inevitably dominate the story of the total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027 . After all, the path of totality crosses Luxor, home to Karnak, the Valley of the Kings, and some of the ancient world's most famous monuments. But follow the moon 's shadow west and another ancient civilization comes into view. Before reaching Egypt, totality will sweep across the Mediterranean and North Africa, passing over an extraordinary collection of Roman cities, fortresses, theaters, temples and triumphal arches. Many lie within what became Rome's North African provinces, a region that produced some of the empire's wealthiest and most impressive cities. From beachside Baelo Claudia in Spain and military Tamuda in Morocco to Timgad and Djémila in Algeria and the jaw-dropping El Jem Amphitheater in Tunisia, Roman ruins will experience between two and more than five minutes of darkness — creating extraordinary possibilities for eclipse chasers and photographers. Gravitational lensing, first predicted by Albert Einstein, occurs when the gravity of a massive foreground object, such as a galaxy or cluster of galaxies, bends, warps, and magnifies the light from a more distant background object. The effect is similar to that of a giant lens in space that allows astronomers to view objects much farther away than any telescope could see on its own. The lenses in this image formed from the precise alignment of a distant background galaxy with the mass of a foreground galaxy, creating distorted and magnified images of the background galaxy that appear as arcs around the foreground galaxy. science.title: Astronomers stunned after James Webb Space Telescope discovers the earliest pair of black hole-powered quasars
science.description: null Using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), astronomers have discovered the oldest pair of supermassive black hole-powered quasars ever seen. There's just one problem: they shouldn't exist! The compact quasar pair, spotted with the aid of the Gemini North telescope, has been designated J1602+4228AB and nicknamed Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua, which means "Two celestial bodies of fathomless powerful darkness in the brilliance of heat reincarnating energy into the universe." The compact quasar pair is seen as it was 900 million years after the Big Bang at a time when such supermassive black holes should not have had time to grow to such tremendous masses. Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua isn't just the oldest and most distant quasar pairing ever seen. There is just 18,100 light-years, or roughly one-fifth the diameter of the Milky Way, between the supermassive black holes, which have masses of 1.5 billion and 400 million times that of the sun. That makes Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua the most compact quasar pair found during a period of the universe's history known as Cosmic Dawn , shortly after the birth of the first stars, galaxies, and black holes. "There is no definitive theoretical explanation for how a single one of these giant quasars exists so early in the age of our universe, much less two," research team leader Silvia Onorato of the NOIRLab said in a statement . "We observed Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua at a time when the universe was only a thirteenth of its age and, astonishingly, its supermassive black holes are just as massive as those we see today." How were supermassive black holes over fed at Cosmic Dawn Quasars occur when the supermassive black holes that sit at the heart of large galaxies are surrounded by a flattened cloud of swirling gas and dust called an "accretion disk," from which they feed or "accrete" matter. The immense gravity of the central black hole causes friction, heating the accretion disk and causing it to glow, often brighter than the combined light of every star in the surrounding galaxy. We see that glow as a quasar. Finding such objects in the recent cosmic history of the 13.8-billion-year-old universe isn't troubling, though finding compact pairs of them is still extremely rare. Such pairs should be common because the merger of galaxies that brings together supermassive black holes is frequent. That should lead to an abundance of pairs of quasars with a separation less than the typical size of a galaxy. There are three reasons this has proven tricky. Firstly, the "quasar phase" of a supermassive black hole is relatively short on cosmic terms. Secondly, even relatively close quasar pairs are very far away, making them faint and hard to detect with ground-based telescopes. Finally, at such great distances and with such a small separation between the two supermassive black holes, the individual members of a quasar pair are hard to individually resolve. science.title: SpaceX launches 2nd mystery mission for US Space Force in 6-day span (video, photos)
science.description: null SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force from California tonight (Nov. 11), the second such flight for the company in a six-day span. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:36 p.m. EST (8:36 p.m. local California time; 0136 GMT on Nov. 12), kicking off a mission called USSF-627. Vandenberg hosted a similar liftoff less than a week ago: On Nov. 6, a Falcon 9 sent the USSF-432 mission skyward from the site, which lies on California's gorgeous but often foggy central coast. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the USSF-627 mission for the U.S. Space Force from California on Nov. 11, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) We don't know much about USSF-627 or USSF-432; both are classified. Some experts have speculated , however, that each mission launched a batch of SpaceX's Starshield satellites for the Space Force's Space Based Sensing and Targeting portfolio, which helps the military branch track potential targets around the world. SpaceX didn't reveal details about either USSF-627 or USSF-432, and the company ended the webcast of both launches shortly after the first stages of their Falcon 9 rockets came back to Earth . In both cases, that touchdown occurred about 8.5 minutes after liftoff on the SpaceX droneship "Of Course I Still Love You," which was stationed downrange of Vandenberg in the Pacific Ocean. It was the seventh mission for USSF-627's Falcon 9 booster, which carries the designation 1103. A Falcon 9 first stage rests on a SpaceX drone ship shortly after launching the USSF-627 mission on Nov. 11, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) Previous Booster 1103 missions NROL-179 | SDA-T1TL-E | SDA-T1TL-A | 3 Starlink missions USSF-627 was the 120th Falcon 9 launch of 2026 and the rocket's 15th national-security flight of the year to date. Eighty-five of the 120 flights have been devoted to building out SpaceX's Starlink broadband constellation in low Earth orbit , which currently consists of more than 11,000 satellites. The Falcon 9 is not on a record-breaking cadence this year. In 2025, the rocket flew a whopping 165 missions , and 122 of them were Starlink flights.
